Subject: Tenant wiring & ops covenant: Redwood private deploy (AresCloud)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is our latest network diagram (v3) and a short description of the tenant footprint. We're preparing for the staging handoff and want to lock down responsibilities and a minimal preflight so both teams know exactly what to validate.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm which party will advertise the egress IP range and whether Redwood will provide a NAT pool (we prefer Redwood-managed to avoid gateway churn).
- BGP vs. VPN: we can do AWS Direct Connect with BGP or IPsec VPN. If BGP is required, share ASN and BGP community requirements.
- MTU and jumbo frames: our edge uses 9001, but we can fallback to 1500 if needed — let us know which you recommend for KV cache replication.
- KMS: we plan to BYOK via our KMS; need exact KMS key ARN format you require and whether HSM attestations are necessary.
- Throughput targets: expected average qPS 600, peak burst 2k qPS. We’ll run a smoke test with 50k tokens/min.

Attachment: ares-network-diagram-v3.pdf (application/pdf, 560KB)

Goal: agree a short "ops covenant" (who owns what) and a 48-hour preflight checklist we can run before production cutover. Can your team propose dates for a dry-run next week?

Thanks,
Samir Shah
Sr SRE, AresCloud

Samir — thanks for the diagram and the clear asks. Copying Ben (on infra intake) and Lauren (customer success) so we have the ops/CS ownership tracked. Below is a proposed mutual action plan and the data points we need from you to finish the preflight template (attached).

Proposed mutual action items (short form):
1) Networking ownership
   - Redwood provides NAT egress pool and publishes the 2 public IPs for allowlist (Redwood owns translation and NACL configuration).
   - AresCloud will configure inbound firewall rules on your side for our control-plane endpoints (we'll provide CIDR and ports).
2) Connectivity
   - If you choose Direct Connect + BGP: provide ASN, primary/secondary BGP peer IPs, and community tags.
   - If IPsec VPN: provide PSK rotation cadence requirements and SPA NAT traversal notes.
3) KMS & keys
   - AresCloud to provide KMS key ARN and key policy snippet. If you require HSM attestation, please confirm vendor and compliance needs.
4) Preflight & smoke test
   - Dry-run date windows: Jul 13-14 (preferred), Jul 16 (backup).
   - Redwood will run a 15-minute token-burst smoke test and a 60-minute sustained traffic window for KV stability.
5) Rollback & monitoring
   - If latency >100ms p50 for 10 minutes during dry-run, we abort and revert routing changes.

Items we still need from AresCloud (please paste into the attached preflight sheet):
- ASN (if BGP) or VPN endpoint details
- Public CIDR(s) for egress allowlist
- KMS ARN + contact for key rotation
- Point of contact for firewall changes and escalation (phone + pager)

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Fri Jul 9 to finalize the checklist if that works for you.

Looping in a couple infra specifics that we should make explicit in the preflight sheet — copy/paste friendly checklist items for the runbook:

- Egress & NAT
  * Redwood will allocate a 2-address NAT pool per tenant. AresCloud must add both IPs to their upstream allowlist.
  * We publish a short-lived DNS name for health checks; please allow outbound DNS from our control plane.
- Routing & BGP
  * If BGP: our ASN is 64512; we will accept private ASNs from your side but prefer public ASN peering where possible. We support MD5 auth for peers.
  * BGP keepalive 60s, holdtime 180s. Community tagging for traffic engineering can be provided on request.
- MTU & fragmentation
  * We recommend 1500 MTU across the tunnel; unless you're doing large frame-sensitive KV replication, jumbo frames increase frag risk on multihop.
- TCP timeouts and healthchecks
  * Our runtime expects stable long-lived TCP connections; please ensure your edge LB timeout >= 600s for control-plane connections.
- Preflight commands (ops)
  * traceroute from your edge to our control-plane public IPs (collect 3 runs)
  * curl health endpoints: https://control.redwood.ai/healthz (expect 200)

I've attached a machine-readable checklist we use during runs — we'll fill the outcomes after the dry-run.

Attachment: preflight-checklist.txt (text/plain, 3KB)

I propose Ben/Infra owns test scaffolding and Redwood will own rollback. Priyom to confirm exact phone/pager contact for Ares.

— Ben
